 Florida Atlantic Coast faces dangerous flooding as intense rain prompts emergency declarations and rescues
 With more rain expected along the Atlantic Coast, Gov. Ron DeSantis expanded an emergency declaration originally issued earlier this month to include Broward County and additional counties facing renewed flooding threats.
 By
 Julian Atienza 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 05:06 Florida's Atlantic coast continues to face heavy downpours, flash flooding 
 Days of heavy rain and storms continue to fuel a large flash flood threat for Florida's Atlantic coast. FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell reports from Rockledge, where snakes are reportedly swimming through flooded streets. 
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 Millions in Florida will be affected by periods of heavy rain and dangerous flash flooding through Saturday.
 Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis announced that hundreds of National Guard members and other state first responders had been mobilized Thursday.
 Flooding has prompted ongoing water rescues, particularly in Broward and Brevard Counties.
 MELBOURNE, Fla. — Florida 's Atlantic Coast is being pounded by relentless rain , which will fuel a dangerous flash flood threat into Saturday, after flooding prompted emergency declarations, widespread road closures and high-water rescues Wednesday.
 ALL EYES ON FUTURE SUBTROPICAL STORM KYLE AS COASTAL STORM BREWS OFF SOUTHEAST THIS WEEKEND 
 The persistent rainfall comes as parts of Florida are still reeling from  deadly, historic flooding along the Space Coast earlier this month.

 With more rain expected along the Atlantic Coast, Gov. Ron DeSantis expanded an emergency declaration originally issued earlier this month to include Broward County and additional counties facing renewed flooding threats.
 Meanwhile, the state is ramping up its response. DeSantis announced Thursday that hundreds of National Guard members and other state first responders had been mobilized, along with 50 high-water vehicles, several airboats and swamp buggies.
 STORM UPDATE: As heavy rainfall impacts communities across Florida, the state is continuing our active response efforts. @FLSERT is mobilizing hundreds of @FLGuard and @FLStateGuard personnel and more than 200 @FLHSMV troopers, along with 235 @MyFWC officers, 50 high-water vehicles and 60 pumps. FWC has also readied 28 ATVs and UTVs, 26 shallow-draft boats, 17 airboats, eight swamp buggies and a Fat Truck. Additionally, 750 @MyFDOT crews are supporting response efforts in impacted communities. The state has also pre-staged more than 6,000 feet of flood control devices, placed shelters on standby and positioned additional emergency resources, including generators and vacuum trucks, for rapid deployment as needed. Florida will continue deploying resources and working alongside local partners to protect residents and respond to the needs of impacted communities. Please continue to follow all guidance from local officials.
— Ron DeSantis (@GovRonDeSantis)  November 19, 2026 The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) also reported that about 235 FWC personnel have been actively responding to affected areas, including helping more than 90 residents at a flooded apartment complex in Broward County.
 In another rescue, first responders were attempting to reach an infant who had stopped breathing when their vehicle became stuck in floodwaters. An FWC officer immediately responded and was able to transport the infant to emergency personnel.

 01:24 Rescue crews deploy specialized trucks as floodwaters swallow Florida roads 
 Heavy rainfall has unleashed dangerous flooding in Hollywood, Florida, swallowing roads and cutting off neighborhoods. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue deployed high-axle rescue vehicles to help local firefighters reach residents in areas inaccessible to standard emergency vehicles.
 Meanwhile, flooding continues to impact communities farther north in Brevard County.
 WHAT ARE FLOOD WATCHES, WARNINGS AND EMERGENCIES? 
 The Brevard County Sheriff's Office told FOX Weather that water rescues are ongoing, with the worst flooding concentrated around  Cocoa , Rockledge and Merritt Island .
 Video from FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell showed inundated roads and neighborhoods in Rockledge on Thursday.
 04:31 FW Correspondent Brandy Campbell: 'Nonstop rain,' widespread flash flooding across Florida coast 
 Nonstop rain is triggering flash flooding in Brevard County, Florida, where roads have been turned into canals. Some neighborhoods are completely inundated, particularly those near the St. Johns River, which remained at major flood stage after historic flooding earlier this month and has now reached a record level near Cocoa. FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell has the latest conditions in Rockledge.
 Officials said communities near the St. Johns River are facing some of the most dangerous conditions as the river has reached an all-time high.
 WEST COAST BRACES FOR RELENTLESS BARRAGE OF STORMS AS POWERFUL ATMOSPHERIC RIVER FUELS HEAVY RAIN, STRONG SURF 
 Law enforcement crews are working to pump water into a nearby canal to prevent additional flooding in residential areas.
 As residents are forced from their homes, Brevard County announced that it opened a shelter Thursday morning at the Walter Butler Community Center for displaced residents. People were asked to bring their own bedding and other supplies.
 HOLLYWOOD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 18: Capt. Jeff Carroll, a law enforcement officer from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, helps Marian Lopez evacuate as floodwaters inundate the neighborhood on November 18, 2026 in Hollywood, Florida. 
 ((Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) / Getty Images) 
 The county also opened a shelter in Melbourne in partnership with the American Red Cross.
 The City of Palm Bay also announced mandatory evacuations for residents of Palm Bay Estates, located west of the canal and east of the railroad tracks, due to ongoing flooding concerns.

— FOX Weather (@foxweather)  November 19, 2026 Homeowners in Cocoa told FOX 35 Orlando that they also had to evacuate after floodwaters breached their homes.
 LAKE MEAD'S CHILLING BARREL DISCOVERY GETS NEW ANSWERS AS OFFICIALS IDENTIFY HOMICIDE VICTIM 
 In addition to the water rescues and evacuations, widespread road closures have been reported in Melbourne , West Melbourne and Palm Bay, according to the Melbourne Police Department.
 BUCKETS OF RAIN DUMPED ON FLORIDA NEIGHBORHOOD: Storms weren't letting up on Florida's Space Coast on Thursday morning, as heavy rain battered a neighborhood. FOX Weather Correspondent Brandy Campbell shared video of a driveway underwater, with water inching up on people's front doors.
— FOX Weather (@foxweather)  November 19, 2026 The widespread flooding first began impacting parts of South Florida Tuesday night, prompting water rescues in  Fort Lauderdale ,  Hollywood  and other parts of Broward County, as well as Miami-Dade County.
 As flooding worsened, Broward County and the cities of Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood declared states of emergency Wednesday.
 00:48 Watch: Drone video shows entire neighborhoods swamped by flash flooding in Broward County, Florida 
 Drone video shows entire neighborhoods swamped by flash flooding in Broward County, Florida, on Nov. 18, 2026.
 The impacts have also disrupted schools across the region. Broward County schools canceled classes for the entire week, while schools in Brevard, Volusia, Indian River and Miami-Dade counties also canceled classes Thursday.
 Officials across South Florida, including the Hollywood mayor, have reported numerous instances of flood damage to homes and businesses.
 HOLLYWOOD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 18: Capt. Jeff Carroll, a law enforcement officer from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, asks a resident if they need help evacuating as floodwaters inundate the neighborhood on November 18, 2026 in Hollywood, Florida.
 ((Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) / Getty Images) 
 The damage was evident Wednesday when the roof of a Hollywood synagogue partially collapsed during the storms.
 FLORIDA GOVERNOR DECLARES STATE OF EMERGENCY AS DEADLY FLOODING GRIPS SUNSHINE STATE 
 Officials said no one was inside the sanctuary of Temple Sinai at the time and no injuries were reported. However, the sanctuary was deemed unsafe amid concerns that more of the roof could give way as additional rain falls.
 01:41 WATCH: Florida synagogue roof gives way after heavy rain 
 A Hollywood, Florida, synagogue that survived decades of hurricanes suffered extensive damage when its roof collapsed during torrential rain Wednesday. No one was inside the sanctuary, and no injuries were reported. Officials deemed the sanctuary unsafe, with concerns that more of the roof could give way as more rain is forecast to fall in Florida. 
 The stalled storm system is combining with easterly  winds  that are funneling a steady stream of moisture into the region, fueling repeated downpours that are expected to continue through Saturday.
